issues.legal_issue: A conviction for cheque dishonour cannot stand where the alleged loan and liability are unsupported by reliable evidence and the defence account is corroborated.
material_facts: The complainant alleged that he had lent money to the accused and that the cheque was issued to repay the loan, but produced no material supporting the alleged loan.
The complainant worked for the accused, had limited annual savings, and gave no account or explanation for how the cheque amount was calculated from the alleged loan.
The complainant did not inquire whether the accused had sufficient funds when the cheque was dishonoured.
Two defence witnesses corroborated the account that the cheque and cash advance related to a proposed land purchase; the complainant did not rebut one witness’s evidence in cross-examination.
The trial court acquitted the accused, but the High Court reversed that acquittal and convicted him.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed, the High Court’s judgment was set aside, and the trial court’s acquittal was restored.
issues.legal_principle: In deciding whether the offence under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 was established, the Court assessed the evidence supporting the alleged liability and the corroborated defence evidence. It relied on Section 138 and cited no earlier cases.

predicates.appeal_from_reversed_acquittal: The proceeding is an appeal by an accused whose acquittal was reversed on appeal.
predicates.complainant_lacks_reliable_support_for_a: The complainant offers no reliable supporting evidence for the alleged debt or liability underlying the cheque.
predicates.defence_account_is_corroborated: Evidence from defence witnesses supports the accused’s alternative account, and that evidence is not effectively rebutted.

issues.definition: When an accused appeals after an acquittal has been reversed, the acquittal is restored if the alleged liability lacks reliable support and the defence account is corroborated.
